question: What is the length of the segment joining (1,2) and (4,6)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Horizontal difference (dx) = 4 − 1 = 3

Vertical difference (dy) = 6 − 2 = 4

The differences form the legs of a right-angled triangle. Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5), the hypotenuse (distance) is directly 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The coordinates of the two points are A(1, 2) and B(4, 6).

**Formula Used:**

Distance d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A (1, 2)
 B (4, 6)
 C (4, 2)
 
 
 dx = 3
 dy = 4
 d = ?

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let (x₁, y₁) = (1, 2) and (x₂, y₂) = (4, 6)

⇒ d = √[(4 − 1)² + (6 − 2)²]

⇒ d = √[3² + 4²]

⇒ d = √[9 + 16]

⇒ d = √25

⇒ d = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Midpoint Formula

The coordinates of the exact midpoint of a segment joining (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) is given by M = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2, (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2).

Section Formula

The coordinates of a point dividing the line segment internally in the ratio m:n are given as ((mx₂ + nx₁) ÷ (m + n), (my₂ + ny₁) ÷ (m + n)).

Distance from Origin

The distance of any point (x, y) directly from the origin (0, 0) simplifies to d = √(x² + y²).
